Best Buy's COGS fell 9.3% vs revenue -10.6% (derived from q_90fe0610bf: revenue $51.761B to $46.298B, COGS $40.121B to $36.386B), a smaller decline that mathematically compresses gross margin. Year-end inventory declined 13.8% (from $5.965B to $5.140B) vs revenue -10.55%, consistent with no year-end build-up. Operating margin fell 1.99 pp (from 5.87% to 3.88%) per edgar.margin_change, exceeding the 1.08 pp gross margin drop by ~0.91 pp, consistent with SG&A deleverage rather than inventory charges.

Truckload freight PPI averaged 164.3 in 2021 and 203.2 in 2022 (peak 211 in Mar 2022 per q_fe3f87cc7f); warehousing PPI averaged 117.4 in 2021 and 135.1 in 2022 (Jan 2023 = 149 per q_3c477d9e81). Both cost pressures were significant in 2022, but peers WMT (-0.96 pp), DG (-0.37 pp), and COST (-0.74 pp) had smaller gross margin declines despite similar cost pressures, consistent with BBY's digital/fulfillment cost structure being more exposed.
